title: Testing punctual purity on mixed-characteristic complete traits
statement:
For a prime $\ell$ and $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, use ordinary small-etale derived categories and Tate twists [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-asd-finite-etale-tate-twist]. If $W$ is a regular Noetherian scheme with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-regular-scheme], say that $W$ is punctually pure at $w\in W$ when, for $W_w=\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{W,w}$, $d_w=\dim\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and its closed-point inclusion $j_w:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(w)\hookrightarrow W_w$, the Kummer fundamental-class map
$$A_{\kappa(w)}\longrightarrow j_w^!A_{W_w}(d_w)[2d_w]$$
of [lem-per-regular-immersion-class-calculus] is an isomorphism. Say that $W$ is punctually pure when this holds at every point. Local rings and residue fields are as in [def-weil-residue-field], affine spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and dimension as in [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring].

A trait here is $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a discrete valuation ring: a Noetherian local domain of dimension one whose maximal ideal is principal. A complete strictly henselian trait has $R$ complete for its maximal-ideal topology and henselian with separably closed residue field (henselian means that every simple root over the residue field of a monic polynomial over $R$ lifts to a root over $R$). Mixed characteristic means that $\operatorname{Frac}R$ has characteristic zero and the residue field has positive characteristic.

Fix $\ell$. Suppose that every integral regular scheme $V$, flat and quasi-projective of finite type over a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait $S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, is punctually pure. Then every regular Noetherian scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible is punctually pure. Here flat and finite type have the meanings of [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and quasi-projective means that $V$ admits a locally closed immersion into $\mathbf P^N_S$ for some finite $N$. No excellence hypothesis is made on $W$.

source.place: Expose XVI, section 3.7 first paragraph, printed p.254 (Fujiwara 2002 Corollary 6.1.5 reduction), with Proposition 3.2.4 (completion invariance) and Proposition 3.2.5 (prime-field/equal-characteristic case), printed pp.244--245. Complete-trait formulation obtained by first completing the strictly henselian regular local test ring.

proof.text: Fix a regular Noetherian $W$ as in the statement and a point $w$. Set $R=\mathcal O_{W,w}$ and $d=\dim R$. By [lem-per-punctual-strict-completion-test], it suffices to prove closed-point purity for $T=\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B=\widehat{R^{\mathrm{sh}}}$ is complete strictly henselian Noetherian regular local of dimension $d$. The cited test applies without excellence of $R$, so no excellence assumption on $W$ has been introduced.

If $B$ contains a prime field, apply [lem-per-prime-field-punctual-purity] to $T$ to obtain the required purity at its closed point. Otherwise $B$ is mixed characteristic $(0,p)$: its residue field has prime characteristic $p$, and the injective map $\mathbf Z\to B$ does not extend to $\mathbf Q$ because $p$ is not a unit. Indeed [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] makes $B$ a domain; if it has positive characteristic it already contains $\mathbf F_p$, and if its residue field has characteristic zero then all nonzero integers are units, giving $\mathbf Q$. In the remaining case $\ell\neq p$ because $\ell$ is a unit.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.2.5 and section 3.7 first paragraph

proof.text: In this remaining case choose a regular system of parameters of $B$. Apply [lem-per-complete-mixed-regular-pair-approximation] to obtain a small directed inverse system $Z_i\hookrightarrow V_i$ over a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait $S$, with limiting pair $\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow T$. The cited statement supplies integral regular affine $V_i$, flat and finite type over $S$, regular $\mathbf F_p$-schemes $Z_i$, and compatible regular sequences of length $d$. Each $V_i$ is quasi-projective as stated there, so the testing hypothesis of the item applies to every $V_i$. It follows that every $V_i$ is punctually pure.

source.place: Agent expansion of XVI section 3.7 complete-trait reduction using I 2.9, I 10.3(i), IV 4.1.8

proof.text: Every $Z_i$ is punctually pure by [lem-per-prime-field-punctual-purity], since it is regular Noetherian over $\mathbf F_p$ with $\ell\neq p$. Apply conditions (b) and (c) of [lem-per-punctual-purity-two-of-three] to $Z_i\hookrightarrow V_i$: condition (b) is this purity of $Z_i$, and condition (c) follows from purity of all of $V_i$ in Step 3. Both schemes are regular Noetherian, and their immersion has constant codimension $d$ by the regular sequence provided in Step 3. Thus the supported Kummer-class map $A_{Z_i}\to i_i^!A_{V_i}(d)[2d]$ is an isomorphism for every $i$.

source.place: XVI Proposition 3.2.3, p.244, and Proposition 3.2.5, p.245

proof.text:
Apply [lem-per-transverse-gysin-limit] to the inverse system from Step 3. Its index is small directed, its schemes and transitions are affine, and its fixed length-$d$ regular sequences are preserved and remain regular at the limit; the limit schemes are $T$ and its closed point. In every degree $q$, the isomorphisms of Step 4 induce compatible isomorphisms
$$H^q(Z_i,A)\longrightarrow H^{q+2d}_{Z_i}(V_i,A(d)).$$
Taking their colimit and using the cited continuity and Kummer-map identification gives
$$H^q(\operatorname{Spec}k,A)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^{q+2d}_{\{t\}}(T,A(d)).$$
This is the map induced by the actual closed-point Kummer class, not merely an abstract isomorphism between the two groups.

source.place: Agent supported-continuity expansion of XVI section 3.7; XVI 2.1, 2.3.1; Stacks 03Q6

proof.text: The residue field $k$ is separably closed. By [lem-exc-etale-sheaves-gsets-point], its small-etale topos is equivalent to sets with an action of its trivial absolute Galois group, hence to sets; therefore global sections on $k$ identify sheaves of $A$-modules with $A$-modules and detect quasi-isomorphisms. Consequently the isomorphisms in every degree from Step 5 say precisely that $A_k\to j_t^!A_T(d)[2d]$ is an isomorphism. The strict-completion test of Step 1 now implies punctual purity of $W$ at $w$. Since $w$ was arbitrary, $W$ is punctually pure.

The item statement is unchanged; testing only over complete traits makes it stronger, not weaker. Step 1: the strict-completion iff (3.2.1 remark + 3.2.4) is true without excellence. Step 2: the case split on characteristic is correct, and the prime-field case is 3.2.5. Step 3: the approximation node is true pure algebra. It uses a Cohen presentation and Popescu on C[x]_(p,x)->C[[x]], not on C->B, which can fail when B is ramified or k imperfect. Cotangent independence gives regular V_i and Z_i; V_i is flat because it is torsion-free; Z_i is an F_p-scheme because p=sum a_j t_j descends. Step 4: two-of-three (b)+(c) gives (a) in codimension d. Step 5: the supported-limit node is true via continuity on the ambient scheme and the complement, plus 2.2.3.1 base change of the Kummer class under a preserved regular sequence. No flatness is needed, so it does not duplicate class-calculus. Step 6: over a separably closed field, RΓ(k,-) is an equivalence, so isomorphisms on every H^q detect the isomorphism. The new nodes are statement-only, sourced, cite no SGA and form no cycle. They do not duplicate completion-supported-constant-comparison (that one assumes excellence), the log-smooth/monomial trait nodes, or the PBC Cohen/Popescu nodes.
